static_traits.name: Lin Na
static_traits.family_status: The youngest child in the family
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems in the past; never received counseling before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, capable of self-reflection; positive attitude toward counseling, high cooperativeness; can describe automatic thoughts and emotional troubles concretely; steady speech pace and tone

basic_info.main_problem: I struggle with feeling inadequate in my ability to learn and excel at playing video games despite my enjoyment of them.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings of inadequacy and self-doubt have started affecting my enjoyment of video games and my overall well-being.

core_beliefs: I lack the ability/perseverance to learn new things

special_situations.event: Making mistakes or hitting difficult levels in games
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot learn quickly and make few mistakes, it means I have no talent / no perseverance
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Increasing practice and repeatedly watching teaching videos to make up and prove myself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am terrible; no matter how I practice, I will not improve

special_situations.event: When comparing himself with others, seeing others improve faster or get stronger with less effort
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my progress is slower than others', it proves I am not good enough, inferior to others
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-reproach; avoids discussing the problem with friends to spare embarrassment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as they are; I simply cannot do it

special_situations.event: When trying to learn new skills, attention focused on mistakes and weaknesses
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only mastering within a short time and maintaining a stable performance counts as qualified; any mistake means failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing only on mistakes and inadequacies, ignoring existing progress and strengths
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not capable enough / not focused enough

special_situations.event: Recalling once clearing a level through persistence, yet still negating that success's meaning
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Sporadic successes do not count; only high overall level deserves recognition
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Downplays achievements, attributing success to luck rather than ability and effort
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: That time was just luck, it does not mean I can learn new things

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen as capable, able to improve, and to gain self-recognition
core_conflict.fear: Fear of appearing incompetent after comparison, being negated and shamed
defense_goal: Lowering the risk of being negated by others by preemptively negating himself through self-criticism and labeling
Avoiding contact with shame emotions through rational interpretations like 'lacking talent / not focused enough'
Avoiding revealing this trouble to friends to avoid embarrassment and potential evaluation

object_relations.self_representation: A learner not good enough, with inadequate ability

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites seeing positive evidence or points out one's strengths (such as strategic ability)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worried acknowledging strengths would be seen as bragging, or unable to change the established impression of 'generally cannot do it'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gentle and supportive tone, first empathizing with his shame and frustration, then guiding him with open-ended questions to concretize evidence; avoiding confrontation, gradually connecting success experiences with self-worth.

manifestations: Reduced sense of enjoyment in games, hard to get fun from them
Overall sense of achievement decreased, motivation declining
Negative experiences generalize from games to other areas of life

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeatedly using self-reproaching labels in sessions (like 'I am terrible' / 'not focused enough' / 'learning slowly')
Generalizing performance as 'I generally cannot do it', hard to let positive information in
Avoids telling friends about troubles out of embarrassment

exception_events.target_problem: When practicing new levels or new skills, the client usually thinks 'no matter how I practice, I will not improve' from frustration and self-doubt, further weakening fun and motivation.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once, she practiced a difficult level for several weeks, finally cleared it successfully, and experienced satisfaction and a sense of achievement, rather than the usual 'magnifying failure'.
exception_events.reason: Clue: adopted sustained, persistent practice; used the strategic thinking they are good at; observed real progress over a longer time span, thereby reducing the pressure of 'immediate results'.

positive_force: Has strengths in strategic thinking and planning (friends ask them for strategy advice)
Has succeeded by persisting to clear levels
Learning investment in proactive practice and watching tutorial videos
Positive attitude toward counseling and willing to try restructuring thinking
Has a few close friends he can talk to about personal problems (potential support)
negative_force: Tending to compare with others and form self-disparagement
Labeling and negating positive evidence (like 'I am terrible' / 'that time was just luck')
Overgeneralization and the preset of 'never improving'
Strongly binding ability performance to self-worth, leading to shame and frustration
Avoids seeking support from friends out of embarrassment

target_behavior.behavior: Strong frustration and self-doubt in gaming and new-skill-learning situations, with self-denying words (like 'I am terrible' / 'I will never get better')
antecedent: Making mistakes or getting stuck while gaming
Watching others progress faster and comparing
Trying new skills, not immediately seeing progress in the short term
target_behavior.core_reason: Equating progress speed with self-worth; mentally filtering and catastrophically interpreting failures and mistakes; using labeling language to negate ability and effort.
target_behavior.function: Escaping uncertainty and failure, gaining a 'controllable interpretation' through self-blame and labels, temporarily easing anxiety about external evaluation.
target_behavior.consequence: Declined fun in games, damaged motivation and achievement, negative experiences generalizing to other life areas, overall decline in sense of well-being
